What the maps contain

MapAround's own offline maps are OpenStreetMap, built every month by my-pipeline in the mapsforge format. This is what they keep: every tag, and the zoom from which the map has it (zoom levels as the app counts them; a style can draw it from later on). Tags marked MapAround are its additions for the outdoors; the others are mapsforge's standard set. What each one means is on the OpenStreetMap wiki (the links).

Made from my-pipeline's tag-mapping.xml (406eefe)

Made by MapAround

  • Marked trails. OpenStreetMap's hiking and foot route relations become lines on their ways: trail=hiking (from zoom 11) with trail_colour (the waymark colour from osmc:symbol or colour: red, blue, green, yellow, black, white, orange, purple, brown, other), trail_offset (their place side by side when up to four colours share a way) and, on the first, trail_n, name and ref.
  • Country borders. The lines of the country border relations get boundary=administrative and admin_level=2 themselves (and disputed=yes on disputed borders), so every map draws them.
  • Kept for the app. smoothness on tracks, and wikipedia and wikidata on places, for the links to their articles.

Every tag
